+# Agent access heatmap overview (preview) - SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
+
+Important
+
+The agent access heatmap is in preview. Features and terminology described in this article might change before general availability.
+
+An agent is only as useful, and as risky, as the content it can reach. As agents become part of everyday work, you need a clear picture of which content they use, so you can keep useful access in place, govern the rest, and scale agents with confidence.
+
+The agent access heatmap gives you that picture. It's a content-first view of agent activity across your Microsoft 365 content, available in the new [Agent governance](agent-governance-overview) node in the SharePoint admin center. For a period you choose, the heatmap shows which SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, and Teams-connected sites agents accessed, which business group owns that content, how sensitive it is, and whether agents only read it or also create and update it. From there, you can drill into a specific site, see which agents use it, and act without leaving the report.
+
+Note
+
+The business group and sensitivity views rely on two features that not every organization uses: business groups (departments) in catalog management and sensitivity labels applied to sites. Organizations that use both get the full heatmap experience. If your organization uses only one, the heatmap shows the view for that one.
+
+## Questions the heatmap helps you answer
+
+Admins tend to start with the same four questions. The heatmap is organized so that each one has a direct answer.
+
+| **Question** | **Where the heatmap answers it** |
+| --- | --- |
+| Which content are agents using? | The dashboard and the heatmap show which SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, and Teams-connected sites agents accessed, and which kinds of agents accessed them. |
+| Whose content is it? | The business group view groups activity by the business group that owns the content. The site view shows who owns each site. |
+| How sensitive is it? | The sensitivity view groups activity by the sensitivity label applied to each site. |
+| Do agents only read it, or also update it? | Actions show the operations agents performed, such as reading, modifying, or uploading files. |
+
+## How the heatmap fits with Microsoft Agent 365
+
+Microsoft Agent 365 is the control plane for agents. It helps you observe, govern, and secure the agents in your organization. The Agent 365 registry tells you which agents you have. The agent access heatmap tells you what content those agents use. Together, they give you an agent-first view and a content-first view of the same activity. You can open the heatmap from the Agent 365 experience or directly from the SharePoint admin center.
+
+The heatmap is one part of [agent governance](agent-governance-overview) in the SharePoint admin center:
+
+| **Capability** | **What it helps you do** |
+| --- | --- |
+| Overview | Get a summary of agent activity across your content and go to the reports and settings you need. |
+| Agent access heatmap | Find where agents access your content, broken down by agent platform, business group, sensitivity, and action. |
+| Settings | Set content guardrails once, on an agent blueprint, so every agent created from that blueprint follows them, including agents created in the future. |
+
+A common pattern is to observe activity with the heatmap, act on a specific site when a finding calls for it, and then set content guardrails so the same intent applies to every agent in scope. Learn more in [View agent activity in the agent governance overview](agent-governance-overview).
+
+## Key concepts
+
+These are the main ideas behind the heatmap. Learn more about report contents and how to work with reports in Generate a report and explore the agent access heatmap.
+
+| **Concept** | **What it means** |
+| --- | --- |
+| Report | A snapshot of agent activity across your Microsoft 365 content for a period you choose. Everything you see in the heatmap comes from a report. Each report reflects your organization's settings at the time it was generated, so you generate a new report to see how activity changes. |
+| Dashboard | Where you explore a report. It summarizes agent activity across your content and contains the heatmap. |
+| Heatmap | A grid with agent platforms as rows and business groups or sensitivity labels as columns. Each cell shows how many sites, OneDrive accounts, and Teams-connected sites agents from that platform accessed. Darker cells mean more. |
+| Agent platform | The kind of agent, such as Copilot Studio agents, agents in SharePoint, or third-party agents. |
+| Views | The business group view shows whose content agents use, based on departments in catalog management. The sensitivity view shows how sensitive that content is, based on the sensitivity labels applied to sites. |
+| Actions | What agents did with the content, such as reading, modifying, or uploading files. |
+| Site view | A single site, with its owner, the agents that use it, and what they did there. |
+| Governance actions | Actions you can take on a site directly from the heatmap, such as restricting content discovery or restricting site access. |
+| Detailed report | A download of the full data behind a report, for analysis outside the SharePoint admin center. |
+
+## Basic scenarios
+
+The following scenarios are a good place to start. Each one takes a few selections from the dashboard.
+
+| **Scenario** | **Where to look** | **Typical next step** |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Find the content agents use most | The dashboard summary, and the heatmap cells with the most resources. | Drill into a site to see which agents use it and what they do there. |
+| Find out whose content agents use | Business group view. | Bring that group's site owners into the review. |
+| Check whether agents use your most sensitive content | Sensitivity view, filtered to your highest labels. | Review the sites and agents with the site owners. Restrict content discovery or site access where agent use isn't expected. |
+| See whether agents only read content or also update it | Actions for each site, in the details pane and the site view. | Confirm with the site owner whether that activity is expected. |
+| Confirm that activity matches what you expect | Rows for agents you expect to be active, such as broadly deployed Copilot agents. | If it matches, no action is needed. Generate reports regularly to see how activity changes. |
+
+Learn more about generating and exploring reports in Generate a report and explore the agent access heatmap.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+Before you start using the heatmap report, make sure you have:
+
+- Microsoft Agent 365 or Microsoft 365 E7 license. For licensing questions, see [Microsoft Product Terms](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2309718) or contact your Microsoft account representative.
+- The [SharePoint Administrator role](sharepoint-admin-role) or the AI Administrator role.
+
+## Get started
+
+You can generate your first heatmap report within a few hours. The steps are:
+
+1. For the full heatmap experience, apply sensitivity labels to your sites and set up business groups in catalog management.
+2. In the SharePoint admin center, expand **Agent governance**, select **Agent access heatmap**, and turn on data collection if it isn't already on.
+3. After data is available, generate a report for the reporting period you want, and then open it to explore the heatmap.
+
+Learn more about each step in Generate a report and explore the agent access heatmap.
+
+## What the heatmap covers
+
+The heatmap shows agent activity on SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, and Teams-connected sites. It includes declarative agents, Agent 365 agents, and Microsoft and third-party agents registered in Microsoft Entra ID.
+
+Keep these points in mind as you use it:
+
+- The heatmap reports on a period you choose. It isn't real-time monitoring.
+- The heatmap is a governance visibility tool. It doesn't replace audit log analysis, per-file diagnostics, or security investigations, and it doesn't show end-user identities.
+- If you use the agent access insights report under **Reports** > **Agent insights**, that report remains available. The heatmap, the business group and sensitivity views, and actions are available in **Agent governance**.
+
+## Related information
+
+- [Agent governance in SharePoint and OneDrive overview](agent-governance-overview)
+- [Monitor agent access to SharePoint and OneDrive](insights-on-agent-access)
+- [Catalog management in SharePoint Advanced Management](catalog-management)
+- [Use sensitivity labels to protect content in Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 groups, and SharePoint sites](/en-us/purview/sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites)
+- [Microsoft Agent 365 documentation](/en-us/microsoft-agent-365/)

+# Generate a report and explore the agent access heatmap (preview) - SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
+
+Important
+
+The agent access heatmap is in preview. Features and terminology described in this article might change before general availability.
+
+This article walks you through preparing your tenant, generating your first report, and using the agent access heatmap to investigate agent activity and act on a specific site. Learn more about what the heatmap shows and the concepts behind it in [Agent access heatmap overview (preview)](agent-access-heatmap-overview).
+
+## Before you begin
+
+The heatmap organizes agent activity by business group and by sensitivity. Organizations that use both business groups in catalog management and sensitivity labels on sites get the full heatmap experience. If your organization uses only one, the heatmap shows the view for that one. The following steps help you check your configuration.
+
+### Licensing and permissions
+
+| **Requirement** | **Details** |
+| --- | --- |
+| License | Microsoft Agent 365 or Microsoft 365 E7 license. For licensing questions, see [Microsoft Product Terms](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2309718) or contact your Microsoft account representative. |
+| Admin role | SharePoint Administrator or AI Administrator. |
+| Sensitivity labels or business groups | Recommended. Use both for the full heatmap experience. See the steps that follow. |
+
+### Step 1: Confirm that sensitivity labels are applied to sites
+
+The sensitivity view uses [Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels](/en-us/purview/sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites) that are applied to sites (container labels). Labels applied only to individual files or emails aren't used. If your organization labels files but not sites, the sensitivity view won't have data to show.
+
+To check your configuration:
+
+1. In the Microsoft Purview portal, confirm that sensitivity labels are enabled for Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 groups, and SharePoint sites, and that at least one published label includes the **Groups & sites** scope.
+2. In the SharePoint admin center, go to **Sites** > **Active sites** and review the **Sensitivity** column. Confirm that your most important sites carry a label.
+
+The more sites that carry a label, the more complete the sensitivity view is. Learn more about setting up container labels in [Use sensitivity labels to protect content in Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 groups, and SharePoint sites](/en-us/purview/sensitivity-labels-teams-groups-sites).
+
+### Step 2: Confirm that business groups are available in catalog management
+
+The business group view uses the **Department** category from catalog management in SharePoint Advanced Management. Catalog management assigns each site to a department based on the Microsoft Entra ID department attribute of the site's owner.
+
+To check your configuration:
+
+1. In the SharePoint admin center, go to **Reports** > **Catalog management**.
+2. Open the **Department** category. Confirm that it lists the groups you expect, such as Finance, Sales, or HR, and that those groups contain sites.
+3. If groups are missing or many sites aren't assigned, update the department attribute for site owners in Microsoft Entra ID. Built-in categories refresh every hour.
+
+Sites whose owners don't have a department value can't be attributed to a business group. Learn more in [Catalog management in SharePoint Advanced Management](catalog-management).
+
+### What to expect based on your configuration
+
+| **Sensitivity labels on sites** | **Departments in catalog management** | **What the heatmap shows** |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Yes | Yes | Business group and sensitivity views. Switch between them at any time. |
+| Yes | No | Sensitivity view only. |
+| No | Yes | Business group view only. |
+| No | No | Neither view. Activity is grouped by site template instead. |
+
+If neither sensitivity labels nor business groups are configured, configure at least one, and then generate a new report.
+
+Tip
+
+Configure sensitivity labels or business groups before you generate a report. Each report reflects the configuration in place when it was generated, so changes you make later appear in the next report you generate.
+
+## Turn on data collection
+
+Reports are built from audit data that's collected after you turn on data collection.
+
+1. Sign in to the SharePoint admin center.
+2. In the navigation pane, expand **Agent governance**, and then select **Agent access heatmap**.
+3. If you're prompted to turn on data collection, turn it on.
+
+Data collection starts when you turn it on, so activity from before that point isn't included. You can generate your first report after 24 hours. For large tenants, it can take up to 48 hours for data to become available. If no report is generated for three months, data collection turns off automatically. You can turn it back on at any time.
+
+## Generate a report
+
+The heatmap is built from a report of agent activity over a period you choose. Report data comes from the Microsoft 365 unified audit log.
+
+1. In the SharePoint admin center, in the navigation pane, expand **Agent governance**, and then select **Agent access heatmap**.
+2. Select **Generate report**.
+3. Select a reporting period: the last 1, 7, 14, or 28 days.
+4. Select **Generate**.
+5. Check the **Status** column to see whether the report is ready. Generation time depends on how much agent activity your tenant has.
+6. When the report is ready, select it to open it.
+
+Keep these points in mind:
+
+- You can have one report for each reporting period at a time, so up to four reports in total. Generating a new report for a period replaces the existing report for that period. To keep the earlier report, download it first.
+- You can generate a new report once every 24 hours.
+
+## Review the dashboard
+
+A report opens on the **Dashboard** tab, which contains the summary cards and the heatmap. The **Report** tab contains the same data in table form.
+
+### Review the summary cards
+
+Summary cards at the top of the report show how many agents accessed your content during the reporting period and how that activity is spread across SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, and Teams-connected sites. If you use sensitivity labels or business groups, you also see activity broken down by each. Select a card to see supporting detail, such as the most active agents and the sites with the most agent activity.
+
+![Screenshot of the Agent governance Overview page with summary cards for total agents, agents accessing resources, and resources accessed by agents.](sharepointonline/media/agent-governance-generate-agent-access-report/agent-governance-summary-cards.png)
+
+### Read the heatmap
+
+The heatmap plots agent platforms against your content.
+
+| **Part of the heatmap** | **What it shows** |
+| --- | --- |
+| Rows | The agent platforms responsible for the most activity, such as Copilot declarative agents, Copilot Studio agents, agents in SharePoint, custom engine agents, and third-party agents. |
+| Columns | Business groups or sensitivity labels, depending on the view you select. |
+| Cells | How many resources (sites, OneDrive accounts, and Teams-connected sites) agents from that platform accessed in that business group or at that sensitivity level. Darker cells indicate more resources. |
+
+To keep the view readable, the heatmap considers the 500 resources with the most agent activity and shows the top five agent platforms and the top five business groups or sensitivity labels, ranked by request volume.
+
+![Screenshot of the Dashboard heatmap showing M365 resources accessed by agents, grouped by Department, with agent platforms as rows and departments as columns.](sharepointonline/media/agent-governance-generate-agent-access-report/agent-access-heatmap-by-department.png)
+
+### Switch views and filter the heatmap
+
+1. Use the view selector above the heatmap to switch between the business group view and the sensitivity view.
+2. Use the filters to choose which business groups, sensitivity labels, and agent platforms appear on the grid.
+
+Tip
+
+Start with sensitivity. Filter to your most sensitive labels first, and then switch to the business group view to see whose content is involved.
+
+## Investigate a cell
+
+Select a cell to open the details pane for that combination of agent platform and business group or sensitivity label. The pane carries forward any filters you applied.
+
+For each resource, the details pane shows the sensitivity label, site template, site owner, number of agents, request volume, and the top actions agents performed. You can pivot the pane to see the same activity in two ways:
+
+| **Pivot** | **What it shows** |
+| --- | --- |
+| By resource | The sites and accounts agents accessed, ranked by request volume. The pane lists the top 100. The full list is available in the detailed report. |
+| By agent | Each agent in the slice, what it accessed, how often, and what it did. |
+
+![Screenshot of the Finance department resources accessed by Copilot Studio agents pane, showing the Overview tab with resources, agent count, sensitivity, and request volume.](sharepointonline/media/agent-governance-generate-agent-access-report/copilot-studio-finance-resource-details.png)
+
+## Understand what agents did
+
+Actions show whether agents only read content or also create and update it. For each agent and resource, the heatmap lists the top three operations recorded in the audit log, such as **FileAccessed**, **FileModified**, or **FileUploaded**, with a count for each.
+
+What counts as expected depends on your organization and on each agent's purpose. Review the actions against what you expect from each agent on each site, and if they don't match, or you aren't sure, check with the site owner.
+
+## Drill into a site
+
+Select a site in the details pane to open the site view. The site view shows who owns the site and lists the top 20 agents that access it by request volume, with each agent's platform and actions.
+
+The site owner usually knows whether an agent belongs with that content, so bring them into the decision before you restrict access.
+
+## Act on a site
+
+You can act on a site directly from the details pane or the site view, without switching to another page.
+
+| **Action** | **What it does** |
+| --- | --- |
+| **Restrict content discovery** | Keeps the site's content from appearing in Microsoft 365 Copilot agent search and discovery. It doesn't change permissions, so people who have access keep it. Changes can take time to take effect, depending on the size of the site. |
+| **Restrict site access** | Limits access to the site to members of the groups you choose. |
+| **View site** | Opens the site. |
+
+To apply an action:
+
+1. In the details pane or the site view, select the site.
+2. Select **Restrict content discovery** or **Restrict site access**.
+3. Review the settings, and then confirm.
+
+Note
+
+After you apply a policy from a report, the policy status in that report doesn't update. To see the current status, select the policy, or open the site from **Sites** > **Active sites** and review its settings. The next report you generate reflects the change.
+
+Site-level actions work well for a specific finding. To apply your intent to every agent in scope, including agents created in the future, use content guardrails on the **Settings** page in **Agent governance**.
+
+## Use the Report tab and download the detailed report
+
+The **Report** tab lists the top 100 sites agents accessed, with each site's sensitivity label and governance settings. You can filter the list, for example by site template, sensitivity label, business group, or whether restricted content discovery or restricted site access is applied. Select a site to see the top 20 agents that access it.
+
+To analyze all of the data, select **Download detailed report**. The download contains up to 1 million rows and includes site details and owner, business group (department), agent ID, name, type, and platform, request volume, operations, site sensitivity, and whether restricted content discovery, restricted site access, and external sharing are enabled for each site.
+
+## What a report includes
+
+Each report captures agent activity for the reporting period you choose. The following table describes what a report includes.
+
+| **Attribute** | **Details** |
+| --- | --- |
+| Reporting period | The last 1, 7, 14, or 28 days. |
+| Activity | Agent activity on SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, and Teams-connected sites, recorded in the Microsoft 365 unified audit log after data collection was turned on. |
+| Agents | Declarative agents, Agent 365 agents, and Microsoft and third-party agents registered in Microsoft Entra ID. |
+| Configuration | Sensitivity labels, business groups, and site policies as they were when the report was generated. Changes you make later appear in the next report you generate. |
+| Request volume | The number of times agents accessed a resource during the reporting period. The heatmap ranks resources, agents, and agent platforms by request volume. |
+| Actions | The operations agents performed on each resource, as recorded in the audit log, such as FileAccessed, FileModified, or FileUploaded. |
+| Detailed report | A download of the full report data, for analysis outside the SharePoint admin center. |
+
+## Limits
+
+The following limits apply to the heatmap and to each report.
+
+| **Item** | **Limit** |
+| --- | --- |
+| Resources in the heatmap | The top 500 by request volume |
+| Heatmap rows and columns | The top five agent platforms, and the top five business groups or sensitivity labels, ranked by request volume |
+| Details pane | The top 100 resources |
+| Site view | The top 20 agents for each site |
+| Report tab | The top 100 sites |
+| Actions | The top three operations for each agent and resource |
+| Detailed report | Up to 1 million rows |
+| Reporting periods | 1, 7, 14, or 28 days, with one report for each period at a time |
+| Report generation | One new report for a period every 24 hours |
+| Coverage | SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, and Teams-connected sites |

+# View Agent Activity in the Agent Governance Overview - SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
+
+The Agent governance **Overview** page in the SharePoint admin center gives you one place to see how agents and Microsoft 365 Copilot use your organization's content. It shows which agents are most active, which sites and content they access most, and how that access breaks down by sensitivity label and department. From the same page, you can go straight to the governance controls that help you reduce oversharing and protect sensitive content.
+
+Note
+
+The agent governance overview is in preview. Features and terminology described in this article might change before general availability.
+
+Use the overview page to:
+
+- Measure agent interaction with content: how many agents in your organization are accessing resources, and how many resources they access.
+- Spot access patterns across the agents, sites, OneDrive accounts, and Teams sites and identify the content with the most agent or Copilot activity.
+- Assess agent actions by evaluating the frequency and amount of sensitive content (by sensitivity label) and which departments own that content.
+- Act on what you find with controls such as restricted access control, restricted content discovery, or open deeper tools such as the agent access heatmap.
+
+![Screenshot of the SharePoint admin center Agent governance Overview page showing agent totals, resources accessed, and resource access patterns.](sharepointonline/media/agent-governance-overview/agent-governance-overview.png)
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+To access the agent governance overview, make sure you have:
+
+- [SharePoint Administrator role](sharepoint-admin-role)
+- Microsoft Agent 365 or Microsoft 365 E7 license. For licensing questions, see [Microsoft Product Terms](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2309718) or contact your Microsoft account representative.
+
+## Open the Agent governance overview page
+
+1. Sign in to the [SharePoint admin center](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2185219) with an account that has the required admin role.
+2. In the left navigation, select **Agent governance** > **Overview**.
+
+## Generate insights
+
+Most of the overview page is empty until you generate insights. Before that, only **Total agents** shows a value, and the other cards say *Available when insights are ready*.
+
+To generate insights:
+
+1. On the **Overview** page, select **Generate insights**.
+2. After generating the report, the page shows the reporting period (for example, **Nov 10–16, 2026 (7 days)**) and a **Generated today** status.
+
+![Screenshot of the Agent governance Overview page with the Generate insights button highlighted and a note that data covers the last 7 days.](sharepointonline/media/agent-governance-overview/generate-insights.png)
+
+Note
+
+Insights cover agent and Copilot activity from the last 7 days.
+
+## What the overview page shows
+
+### Agents and resources at a glance
+
+This section summarizes agent activity across your organization.
+
+| Card | What it shows | Where it takes you |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Total agents | The number of agents in your organization, as of the date shown. You see this value before you generate insights. | View agent information in the registry: opens the agent registry, where you can see details about each agent. |
+| Agents accessing resources | The number of agents that accessed SharePoint, OneDrive, or Teams resources during the reporting period. | View top 100 agents: a list of the most active agents. |
+| Resources accessed by agents | The number of resources across SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams those agents accessed during the reporting period. | View top 100 resources: a list of the most-accessed resources. |
+
+> 
+> **Tip:** Compare **Agents accessing resources** with **Total agents** to see what share of your agents actively use organizational content.
+
+### Resource access patterns
+
+This section shows where agent and Copilot activity is concentrated, so you can focus on your governance work where it matters most.
+
+![Screenshot of the Resource access patterns section in the SharePoint admin center Agent governance overview, showing top agents, top resources, sensitivity label, and department cards.](sharepointonline/media/agent-governance-overview/resource-access-patterns.png)
+
+| Card | What it shows | Next step |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Top agents accessing resources | The agents that made the most resource access requests, with the agent type (for example, Copilot Studio agent) and the number of requests. | Select an agent for details, or select View top 100 agents. |
+| Top resources accessed by the most number of agents | The sites and accounts accessed by the largest number of different agents, with the resource type (for example, Communication site, OneDrive account, or Group connected site) and the agent count. | Select a resource for details. |
+| Top resources accessed by Microsoft 365 Copilot | The resources that Microsoft 365 Copilot used most, including sites, OneDrive accounts, and Teams chats, with the number of requests. | Select a resource for details, or select View agent access report. |
+| Most accessed resources by sensitivity label | The sensitivity label most common on the resources agents access (for example, Highly confidential), and how agent-accessed resources are distributed across labels. | Select View agent access by sensitivity. |
+| Most accessed resources by department | The department that owns the most agent-accessed resources (for example, Finance), and how agent-accessed resources are distributed across departments. | Select View agent access by department. |
+
+### Dive deeper and take action
+
+The card at the top right of the page highlights related tools. Use the arrows to move between them.
+
+| Tool | What it does | Get started |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Agent access heatmap | Shows every agent, site, and sensitivity label in one view, so you can spot high-activity combinations at a glance. | Select **Open heatmap**, or select **Agent governance** > **Agent access heatmap**. |
+| Permission insights report | Shows which sites an agent user has permission to access. | Select **Generate report**. |
+
+### Available actions
+
+The **Available actions** bar at the bottom of the page suggests governance controls you can apply based on what you see. Use the arrows to move between them, and select **Learn how** to read more about each one.
+
+| Action | Use it to |
+| --- | --- |
+| Restricted access control | Limit a site to only the people who need it. Agents acting on behalf of users can't reach content on the site for users outside the allowed group. |
+| Restricted content discovery | Control whether content from specific SharePoint sites can be discovered by Copilot and organization-wide search. |
+| Site access review | Ask site owners to confirm who should still have access to their sites. |
+
+## Give feedback
+
+Each section on the overview page includes **Is this section useful?**. Select thumbs up or thumbs down to tell us whether the insights help you.
+
+## FAQ for agent governance
+
+**Why are most cards empty?**
+
+Insights aren't generated automatically. Select **Generate insights** to fill the page with data from the last seven days.
+
+**What time period do the insights cover?**
+
+Insights cover the last seven days before you generated the insights. The date range appears under the page title. If you created an agent access heatmap previously, the most recent report data appears on the overview page.
+
+**Which resources are included?**
+
+SharePoint sites, OneDrive accounts, and Teams resources (such as Teams chats).
+
+## Related information
+

+- [Data access governance reports](data-access-governance-reports)

+# Restrict content collaboration by agentic users (preview) - SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
+
+Prevent agents from sharing Microsoft 365 content outside your organization.
+
+Agentic users, also known as agents with identities, increasingly work alongside the people in your organization. An agentic user emulates human capabilities and handles complex tasks, operating much like a virtual employee. As part of Microsoft Agent 365, every agentic user gets its own identity in Microsoft 365, including a mailbox, a OneDrive account, and Teams chat.
+
+Like people, agentic users can be granted access to SharePoint sites and Microsoft 365 resources, and they can share that content with others in your organization. To prevent agentic users from oversharing content broadly, admins can enforce a content guardrail. With the content guardrail turned on, SharePoint Administrators can allow agentic users to share SharePoint and OneDrive content and collaborate with a limited set of users.
+
+Note
+
+This feature is in preview. In this release, an agentic user’s allowed list contains only its agent manager, so when the setting is on, the agentic user can share a site and its contents with only its manager. The guardrail is off by default.
+
+You can apply this setting to all agent blueprint app IDs in your tenant or only to the blueprint app ID that you select. Because the setting lives on the blueprint app ID, every agentic user associated with the blueprint honors it, including third-party agent blueprint app IDs.
+
+## When to use this setting
+
+Use the setting when the agentic users of a specific agent blueprint ID should not share content with anyone other than its manager. Common scenarios include:
+
+- Rolling out a new agent blueprint app ID while you evaluate how its agentic users handle organizational content.
+- Meeting compliance requirements in regulated industries, such as financial services, where agentic users have access to restricted or proprietary content.
+- Deploying an assistant for a team that handles high-value material, such as deal or legal content, so that what the agent gathers stays with the person accountable for it.
+
+For example, a SharePoint Administrator at Contoso activates the Sales Agent blueprint and turns on the setting for it. Every agentic user associated with the Sales Agent blueprint app id, can now share sites and content only with its own agent manager. If a sales agent user tries to share a proposal with anyone else in the organization, the share is blocked.
+
+## How the setting works
+
+This setting works at the tenant level. Turn it on for agent blueprint app ID, either in the Microsoft Agent 365 portal when you onboard a blueprint app ID or in the SharePoint admin center under Agent governance.
+
+| Scope | What happens |
+| --- | --- |
+| Agentic users of specific blueprints | Only agentic users associated with the blueprint app ID you select are restricted. Agentic users of other blueprints follow your existing sharing settings. Blueprint app ID can be first-party (Microsoft) or third-party agentic applications. |
+
+When an agentic user tries to share a site or its content, the recipients are checked and share with anyone other than the agent’s manager is blocked.
+
+The guardrail is designed to be safe to turn on broadly:
+
+- It isn’t retroactive. Content an agentic user shared before you turned on the setting stays shared, and no existing permissions are removed.
+- It fails closed. If the circle of work can’t be evaluated, the share is blocked and the failure is logged.
+- It works alongside other existing content governance controls. Information barriers, Restricted Access Control, and sensitivity labels still apply.
+
+Note
+
+The guardrail is applied at the tenant level for each blueprint. Site-level controls aren’t currently available.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+Before you turn on the guardrail, make sure that you have:
+
+- The SharePoint Administrator role.
+- Microsoft Agent 365 or Microsoft 365 E7 license. For licensing questions, see [Microsoft Product Terms](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2309718) or contact your Microsoft account representative.
+- Identified the agent blueprints you want to restrict. If you plan to scope the guardrail to specific blueprints, have each blueprint’s name or ID (GUID) ready.
+
+## Turn on the guardrail
+
+### In the Microsoft Agent 365 portal
+
+Global Administrators can turn on the guardrail as one of the default protection policies applied when an agent template is onboarded in the tenant. In the Agent 365 portal, go to **Policies**, open **Default protection for autopilots**, and select the setting to be **On**.
+
+When you set the guardrail to **On**, every agent user associated with the agent template can share site and content only with their manager.
+
+[![Screenshot of the Default protection for autopilots Policies tab in Microsoft admin center with Restrict collaboration by agentic users turned On.](media/agentic-users-governance-restrict-share-to-set-users/restrict-agent-collaboration.png)](sharepointonline/media/agentic-users-governance-restrict-share-to-set-users/agent-365-policies-autopilot-protections.png#lightbox)
+
+## Agentic user guardrail FAQ
+
+### Is the policy turned on by default?
+
+No. The guardrail is off by default. Agentic users follow your existing sharing settings until you turn it on.
+
+### Does the policy affect people in my organization?
+
+No. The restriction applies only to agentic users. People in your organization continue to share content according to your tenant and site sharing settings.
+
+### Can I apply the policy to individual sites?
+
+Not currently. Configure the guardrail at the tenant level, either for all agent blueprints or for the specific blueprints you select.
+
+### Which agentic applications can I restrict?
+
+You can restrict agentic users associated with both first-party (Microsoft) and third-party agentic application blueprints.
+
+### Who is in an agentic user’s circle of work?
+
+In this release, an agentic user’s circle of work contains only its agent manager.
+
+### What happens to content an agentic user already shared?
+
+Nothing changes for content shared before you turned on the guardrail. Existing shares and permissions stay in place; the guardrail applies to new sharing actions.
+
+### Does the guardrail replace my other sharing controls?
+
+No. Your tenant and site sharing settings, information barriers, Restricted Access Control, and sensitivity labels continue to apply. When more than one policy applies, the most restrictive one wins.
+
+## Related information
+

+- [Manage sharing settings for SharePoint and OneDrive in Microsoft 365](turn-external-sharing-on-or-off)
+- [Permission insights for agentic users](agent-governance-overview)

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft OneDrive for iPad: Presentation mode for PDFs
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft OneDrive for iPad will introduce a presentation mode for PDFs, enabling a focused, view-only experience that disables free scrolling to prevent accidental page changes. Rolling out worldwide in December 2026, it is enabled by default with no admin controls required and does not affect file permissions or compliance.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

We are introducing presentation mode in the Microsoft OneDrive app for iPad. Users can select a new Presentation button in the PDF viewer to enter a focused, view-only experience that prevents free gesture scrolling between pages, reducing accidental page changes while presenting without requiring users to move the file to another app. This update is based on customer feedback requesting a presentation experience directly in the OneDrive PDF viewer. This feature is not available on iPhone.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by late December 2026.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Users who open and present PDF files in the OneDrive app for iPad.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft OneDrive for iPad

What will happen

  • Users can select the Presentation button in the OneDrive PDF viewer to enter presentation mode.

  • Presentation mode supports all PDFs, displays them in a view-only experience without editing controls, and does not intentionally change them or create a new copy.
  • Free scrolling or swiping between pages is disabled in presentation mode, preventing accidental page changes. Users can switch pages only by selecting the on-screen navigation buttons.
  • The feature is enabled by default for all OneDrive for Business customers.
  • No admin control or tenant configuration is available for this feature.
  • Presentation mode changes how a PDF is displayed during a presentation and does not intentionally change file storage, permissions, sharing, retention, or audit behavior. Existing OneDrive access permissions and protections applied to the PDF continue to apply.

Action required and recommendations

No administrative action is required before rollout. We recommend that you inform helpdesk and support teams about the new presentation experience and update internal user guidance for presenting PDFs from the OneDrive app for iPad.

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft OneDrive for Windows and Mac: node_modules folders will be excluded from sync by default
messageCenterItems.summary: Starting December 14, 2026, OneDrive for Windows and Mac will exclude new folders named "node_modules" from syncing by default to improve performance. Existing synced folders remain unaffected. Administrators can disable this exclusion via policy if needed. No user prompts will occur, and local folder use continues.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

We are updating the OneDrive sync app for Windows and Mac to exclude new folders named node_modules from syncing by default, beginning December 14, 2026. This change extends OneDrive's existing default exclusion list, which includes .db-wal files, as mentioned in MC1457838 on October 5, 2026.

JavaScript and Node.js projects can generate tens of thousands of small dependency files in node_modules folders. This change is intended to improve sync performance and reduce unnecessary storage and bandwidth usage. Developers can rebuild these folders using their package manager.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin on December 14, 2026, and is expected to complete by mid-January 2027.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Users with work or school accounts who create node_modules folders in OneDrive-synced locations, including Desktop and Documents folders managed through Known Folder Move.

Platforms and services

  • OneDrive for Windows
  • OneDrive for Mac

What will happen

  • New node_modules folders: OneDrive will exclude newly created folders named node_modules from syncing by default. These folders will remain on the device and will not upload to OneDrive.
  • Folder name matching: The exclusion applies to folders named exactly node_modules, regardless of capitalization.
  • Existing node_modules folders: Folders that are already syncing will continue to sync. OneDrive will not remove existing content from the cloud or devices.
  • User experience: Users will not receive prompts. Excluded folders will continue to function locally but will not be available through OneDrive on the web or other devices.
  • Administrative controls: Administrators can use existing OneDrive sync policies to turn off the default exclusion list if their organization needs these folders to sync.

Action required and recommendations

No action is required if your organization wants to use the new default behavior. If your organization needs node_modules folders to continue syncing, configure the appropriate OneDrive sync policies before December 14, 2026.

We recommend that you update your helpdesk and developer guidance to reflect the new default behavior and notify developers who maintain code projects in OneDrive-synced locations.

Learn more

  • Deploy and configure the OneDrive sync app for Mac - SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
  • IT Admins - Use OneDrive policies to control sync settings - SharePoint in Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
